newsitem.title: UK: Bass plans to sell 200 pubs - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bass plans to sell 200 pubs - paper.

text.p: Brewing group Bass Plc is in talks to sell 200 outlets to pub entrepreneur Michael Cannon, the Observer newspaper reported.
The paper said selling the pubs could help allay competition concerns from Britain's Office of Fair Trading (OFT) over Bass's plans to buy Allied-Domecq's 50 percent stake in Carlsberg-Tetley.
However, the newspaper said it was believed that the pubs' sale to Cannon will go ahead even if Bass was not allowed to proceed with the Carlsberg-Tetley deal.
Cannon was expected to pay 40 million stg for the pubs, although any sale was likely to be conditional on his agreement that the pubs continue to stock Bass beers.

Bass's plans to buy into Carlsberg-Tetley and then merge operations with its existing brewing business are being investigated by OFT, which could refer the 200 million stg deal to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
The newspaper said Bass will be told to give up control of 1,000 leased pubs and give up two of its beer brands if it is to be allowed to go ahead with the takeover.
A spokesman for Bass said the company declined to comment on the report.
